headline: Lowest pay raised by record 142% in new national pay scale
summary: Government employees will receive arrears from July 1, as the new 2026 pay scale doubles basic salary for top officials and significantly boosts lowest pay.
details: The Ministry of Finance has issued a gazette notification implementing the National Pay Scale 2026 retrospectively from July 1, with employees receiving arrears for the period between July 1 and the order's issuance.
This marks the largest pay hike for the civil service since independence, doubling the basic salary of top officials and increasing the lowest pay by a record 142 percent.

Basic salary adjustments will be implemented in phases. For employees in Grades 10 to 20, 50% of the total increase will be added from July 1 to December 31, 2026, rising to 75% from January 1, 2027, and reaching 100% by July 1, 2027.
For officials in Grades 1 to 9, 40% of the total increase will be disbursed from July 1 to December 31, 2026, and 70% from January 1, 2027, before reaching full adjustment by July 1, 2027.
All other allowances will continue at existing rates drawn as of June 30, 2026, until December 31, 2027, with revised allowance rates taking effect on January 1, 2028.
The previous national pay scale introduced in 2015 had seen basic pay rise by 95% in the top grade and 101% in the2015 scale.
caption:
A record 142% increase for the lowest pay! Government employees are set for the largest pay hike since independence.

The Ministry of Finance has issued a gazette notification implementing the National Pay Scale 2026 retrospectively from July 1, with employees receiving arrears for the period between July 1 and the order's issuance.

This marks the largest pay hike for the civil service since independence, doubling the basic salary of top officials and increasing the lowest pay by a record 142 percent.

Basic salary adjustments will be implemented in phases. For employees in Grades 10 to 20, 50% of the total increase will be added from July 1 to December 31, 2026, rising to 75% from January 1, 2027, and reaching 100% by July 1, 2027.

For officials in Grades 1 to 9, 40% of the total increase will be disbursed from July 1 to December 31, 2026, and 70% from January 1, 2027, before reaching full adjustment by July 1, 2027.

All other allowances will continue at existing rates drawn as of June 30, 2026, until December 31, 2027, with revised allowance rates taking effect on January 1, 2028.

The previous national pay scale introduced in 2015 had seen basic pay rise by 95% in the top grade and 101% in the2015 scale.

headline: 13-year-old boy's body recovered from jungle in Comilla
summary: Aprotim, the son of a Comilla University teacher, went missing after leaving home to take photos with his mother's iPhone; his body was found in the Lalmai Sananda Hill area.
details: The body of 13-year-old Aprotim, a student of Comilla Border Guard Public School, was recovered from the Lalmai Sananda Hill jungle area adjacent to the Comilla University campus.
Aprotim had gone missing on Friday afternoon after leaving his home in the Kotbari area of Comilla to take photos with his mother's iPhone.
His father, K M Firoz Shahriar, had filed a General Diary (GD) at the Comilla Sadar South Model Police Station after the boy failed to return home.
Comilla Police Superintendent Mo. Asaduzzaman stated that police are working non-stop to identify the actual killers and arrest them. He noted that one person has been detained for questioning.
The SP mentioned that the boy's location, the detainee's mobile and technical data, and CCTV footage are being analyzed to uncover the motive and the perpetrators.
The boy's mother, Dr. Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, is devastated, demanding answers and justice for her own child's death.
caption:
A 13-year-old boy went missing while taking photos with an iPhone and was later found dead in a jungle.

The body of 13-year-old Aprotim, a student of Comilla Border Guard Public School, was recovered from the Lalmai Sananda Hill jungle area adjacent to the Comilla University campus.

Aprotim had gone missing on Friday afternoon after leaving his home in the Kotbari area of Comilla to take photos with his mother's iPhone.

His father, K M Firoz Shahriar, had filed a General Diary (GD) at the Comilla Sadar South Model Police Station after the boy failed to return home.

Comilla Police Superintendent Mo. Asaduzzaman stated that police are working non-stop to identify the actual killers and arrest them. He noted that one person has been detained for questioning.

The SP mentioned that the boy's location, the detainee's mobile and technical data, and CCTV footage are being analyzed to uncover the motive and the perpetrators.

The boy's mother, Dr. Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, is devastated, demanding answers and justice for her own child's death.
